reviews.text: A place where love for animals reigns supreme. I want to thank everyone, from the receptionists to the nurses, to Dr. Principi, who has put up with and supported me throughout this difficult journey, even responding on holidays and at odd hours, to Dr. Mariani, who was the first to immediately identify the problem during an emergency room visit and took action with all the tests, CT scans, and everything else to fully understand the situation, up until yesterday with the final farewell to my beloved Blanco, a professionalism, kindness, and empathy I have not encountered anywhere else! Thank you, truly thank you for everything you have done for me and my Blanco!
I sincerely thank the clinic for their hospitality, their willingness to quickly perform an analysis I urgently needed despite it being a holiday, and the kindness of Mrs. Fabiana!

Disappointed, bitter, and sad: that's how I left the emergency room on Wednesday night. I'm sharing my experience that night; my goal isn't to judge a specialist's expertise, but to recount an episode.
Around 9:30 PM, I called the clinic and explained that my cat was sick: abdominal pain, loss of appetite, and watery vomiting. I said I suspected she'd ingested something (perhaps a tourniquet, since she's obsessed with them), and asked, "Can I take her there? Can you DO anything?"
They told me to bring her in right away. I arrived at 10:00 PM; I waited in the waiting room.
At 12:30 PM, they examined my cat; the visit lasted 4 minutes. The doctor took her temperature and said she had one, palpated her abdomen and said she was in pain (just as I'd said on the phone). He tells me the only thing he can do is TRY AN ULTRASOUND, but that wasn't his job description (?) and that the results should wait for the specialist to be available the next afternoon. He tries a "rough" ultrasound and says that "MAYBE it could be a foreign body," but reiterates that it should be the sonographer who says so. I ask if it's possible to get a diagnosis, but no, it's a HYPOTHESIS that needs to be verified and not a diagnosis (a hypothesis I had first formulated independently at home AND WHICH I HAD EXPOSED hours earlier!!!).
So I ask what should be done, and he tells me the cat should be left hospitalized for an ultrasound the next afternoon; I say that I wouldn't leave the cat there alone all that time to receive a diagnosis, in the best-case scenario, THE AFTERNOON OF THE NEXT DAY.
He tells me to wait WITHOUT TELL ME WHY; I waited a little longer, then, impatiently, went to the reception desk and told them I was taking the cat away, making it clear I was in a hurry because I wanted to take her somewhere else. The doctor arrived, visibly nervous (it was probably a particularly busy evening) and told me she wanted to prescribe something for the cat (I let her know how disappointed I was, given that there was no diagnosis; she could have been given a painkiller, perhaps, but that was the end of it...).
I paid what I thought was a high fee for a temperature measurement and abdominal palpation (she told me that the "ultrasound" wasn't included, because "that wasn't her job," and so I wasn't given the results of her attempt, rightfully so). She told me I had to sign the waiver of liability, which stated that despite the diagnosis, I was refusing to be admitted (what diagnosis? Wasn't that just a hypothesis?!) I specifically stated in the document that there was no diagnosis, which was why I was leaving to seek a diagnosis elsewhere, followed by EMERGENCY treatment.
Summary? I was there for 3 hours for a 3-minute visit with no diagnosis.
I went to another clinic. They did blood tests, took her temperature (which she actually didn't have!!!), an ultrasound, a failed attempt to make her vomit the foreign body, and removed it via endoscopy. The cat was discharged in 4 hours.
Just to say that an emergency room must have the resources and means to provide a service worthy of an EMERGENCY ROOM.
I repeat, my situation probably wasn't a "red code," and I'm not judging the doctor's professionalism IN GENERAL—I don't have the expertise to do so—but I'm sharing my experience THAT evening, hoping it will be seen as an opportunity to improve a service that is important to those who come to you.

They saved our dwarf rabbit Lilith, they truly saved her with an emergency operation. The attention and humanity of the entire staff is fantastic. They are helpful and knowledgeable. Trust them with confidence. Excellent exotic care. The prices for their services are very fair.
Excellent facility. I've had several specialist visits, and the doctors are very good. I'll continue to follow them.

A heartfelt thank you to the entire Polivet Hospital in Rome - Salaria - for saving my poodle Leontine from the very dangerous Pyometra in the middle of August.
An excellent team:
Ultrasonographer Margherita Zingone;
Anesthesiologist Ilaria Miraglia;
Surgeon Dario Mselli
and the entire admissions staff. Thank you!
You have demonstrated not only extraordinary professional competence, but
also a profound empathy that I will never forget.
There are not enough words to thank you.
My husband and I are deeply grateful for your commendable work and for the support you have given us.
Leontine is now well and a happy dog ​​despite her 15 years.
💞🙏🐾

I don't recommend this facility. My cat came home terrified, almost afraid of me and constantly has his chin in the water. Three days of hospitalization, a lot of money spent, and in the end, no one gives an explanation for what the cat has... they ask for test after test, which is incredibly expensive. I even had to go to the pharmacy to buy enemas. It's all so absurd.

Thanks for your review from all the Polivet staff! 😊

They were kind enough to advise me over the phone on what and how to treat my turtle's leg, which then healed in a few days 🥰🥰 …
Always very kind and helpful, as well as professional...
Very professional
I recommend him for his seriousness and professionalism!!!
I found a welcoming environment and a competent and very human staff. What struck me was the tranquility I noticed in our four-legged friends!!! I highly recommend it. Thanks from Dodo❤️

We thank you for the treatment and sensitivity shown in this difficult occasion for us.
Excellent experience. Dr. Spiga was able to combine expertise and empathy in caring for my dog.

There are no words to describe absolute excellence.
After months of useless and harmful therapies for my cat in another practice, Polivet established the right treatment, performed instrumental tests, and quickly followed surgery, saving my beloved cat.
EVERYONE—and I mean EVERYONE—were extremely knowledgeable, generous with explanations, and empathetic.
My immense gratitude and admiration to them.
Marzia Mannias

A truly unique clinic, in my opinion. We had a very serious problem with our Trachemys tortoise, who had ingested some pebbles from the aquarium and was in serious danger. Dr. Maria Granata dedicated herself to her, and with perseverance and valuable advice, she was back to her former self within a month. Thank you so much, because we didn't think she could get through this. Our tortoise is now healthier than ever. I recommend this doctor to anyone who has exotic pets like us.

I brought my dog ​​with a very bad leg, and we were cared for for months with the utmost kindness and compassion. I especially want to thank Dr. Paragnani and Catanalotto for their professionalism and patience in caring for us and for managing to resolve such a complex situation.

Dear Lucrezia,
We regret the rating you chose to leave us, especially in the absence of a comment that would allow us to understand the reasons behind it.
However, we have reviewed the case to which we believe your rating may apply. The dog, which you boarded, was a very geriatric patient, suffering from various issues and in severe pain. After the examination and initial tests, the veterinarian determined that, given his condition, even palliative care was not possible to guarantee him an adequate quality of life.
The situation was then discussed by telephone with the owner, who, understanding the severity of his condition, authorized compassionate euthanasia. Since she was away on vacation and unable to be present in person, she instructed you to accompany the dog and proceed on her behalf. The decision was therefore shared and authorized by the owner, with her presence at the facility as a family representative.
In light of what we have reconstructed, we sincerely do not understand what led to your negative rating. If you'd like to share your motivations with us, we'd be happy to listen and discuss what happened in more detail.
Best regards,
The PoliVet team

Hi, my dog ​​was attacked by a Pitbull and we went to the emergency room late at night. They welcomed us with the best care for both us and the dog. They have a unique passion for animals. Imagine, the surgeon was about to leave the room, already changed at the door, and as soon as he saw our dog, he immediately went back inside to manage the situation. I don't think other places and people would do this. Excellent experience!!!

NO ORGANIZATION AND NO EMPATHY.
I went to this clinic last night with my dog, and what I saw was unacceptable for a 24-hour emergency room.

In the waiting room, there was a woman with a bleeding dog that had been mauled by two Maremma Sheepdogs. After more than an hour of waiting, during which the staff completely disappeared, leaving the room empty, around 1:00 a.m. the vets came out saying they couldn't do anything because they were too busy. They told the woman to take the dog to another clinic.

Leaving a bleeding dog waiting for an hour and then sending him away in the middle of the night without even providing first aid is extremely serious.

Bianchino (15 years old) was hospitalized in serious condition in December 2025, and was diagnosed with severe kidney failure with very high values ​​(CrCl at 27!). The doctors rightly told us we could try to keep him in the clinic, but that there wasn't much hope.

Despite this, Bianchino exceeded all expectations; he began to improve during his hospitalization, and both the doctors and nurses treated him with love. They updated us on his progress every day, and after two weeks of hospitalization, he was able to go home.

Months have passed since that episode, and Bianchino is still here with us, still suffering from kidney failure but now under control, and enjoying his new life in Calabria.
I thank the entire team for saving him and giving me more time with him ❤️.
Welcoming, easy to reach facility... the medical and paramedical staff are empathetic and helpful... what can I say about the reception... patient, kind and welcoming... thanks again

I'm writing this review after an extremely negative and concerning experience with the clinical management of my 14-year-old dog, who suffers from epilepsy and is undergoing stable treatment. I brought him in for markedly swollen mandibular lymph nodes; since the previous evening, he had also been refusing food and water.
The discharge form lists "anorexia" as the reason for admission, a definition that doesn't match the reason for admission, although it does list the suspected diagnosis as "Lymphadenopathy of the retromandibular lymph nodes, nature to be determined."
I find the discharge statement, "Alert and reactive," even more serious. My videos, however, show the dog unable to stand, with his head hanging, his tongue hanging out, and evident weakness, which was also noted by the subsequent clinic.
Another serious aspect concerns the oral examination.
The dog presented with significant halitosis, increasing difficulty eating hard foods, and swollen mandibular lymph nodes. When I asked, I was told, in front of others, that the mouth had not been examined because it was deemed unnecessary.
With swollen mandibular lymph nodes and feeding difficulties, I believe an oral exam is not secondary.
I was offered a cytology exam under sedation. I asked if, given the epilepsy and chronic medication, the referring neurologist had been involved; I was told that the clinic does not contact other veterinarians. In front of others, the epilepsy diagnosis and the long-term medication were also questioned.
The recommendations, however, include an "oral cavity examination" and cytology under sedation. I therefore want to clarify one point. After losing confidence in the evaluation, I chose not to authorize other procedures and instead arranged the transfer. In the meantime, I asked that the dog be monitored and kept stable. It was a Saturday, in August, and the options were limited, but I arranged the transfer as soon as possible.
During his hospital stay, I didn't receive the promised updates: I always had to call and was often told the staff was busy with other emergencies.
Transferred to another facility, the dog was reevaluated and given the necessary tests, with a diagnostic process consistent with his clinical picture.
I question the method, the perceived superficiality, the lack of attention to my reports, and the lack of communication. I paid €634, and the dog was returned to me, as documented, in much worse condition. I find it unacceptable that the report describes him as "alert and responsive" when the videos show the opposite. This is not the care I expect from a veterinary facility, much less an emergency room.
A veterinary emergency room is no substitute for a doctor who knows the animal's medical history and treatments. In complex cases, with chronic conditions and ongoing care, I believe a discussion between professionals is desirable to reconstruct the situation and evaluate the most appropriate course of action.
Based on my experience, I absolutely do not recommend this facility.
AND YOU ARE RIDICULOUS WITH THE REVIEWS THAT IMMEDIATELY FOLLOW THE NEGATIVES AND THE POSITIVES... WHAT STRANGE COINCIDENCES...
P.S. = Do you even have the courage to respond? The doctor was called after I insisted. I won't even respond to the rest because you're embarrassed. You should just be ashamed. This is one of the many videos I made the day I left the clinic to take him to a reputable facility! Does this look like a dog discharged in an alert and responsive state? Shame on you!!! SHAME ON YOU!!!!

I visited this clinic on Ferragosto (August 15th), during an extremely difficult time when my dog, now very elderly, had to leave us.
Despite the painful circumstance, I was deeply touched by the extraordinary kindness, professionalism, and empathy demonstrated by all the staff: from the person who answered the phone with such kindness, to the two ladies at the reception desk, to the veterinarian who cared for my dog ​​with immense kindness and respect.
There are details that make all the difference and bring comfort when facing difficult moments, such as saying goodbye to a dog who has been your friend for 14 years: the room reserved for us overlooked a meadow with a river, allowing my dog ​​to experience the last image of his life of a serene and open nature. Furthermore, I found the price absolutely fair and honest, especially considering it was a public holiday like Ferragosto.
If it were possible, I would give an even higher rating than the maximum expected. I sincerely thank all the staff for helping us navigate this moment in the most humane and dignified way possible.

NEVER AGAIN! I'm speechless, I don't even intend to set foot in there again, not to mention the excuses they've given me... But then 80 euros for just touching the cat... Disgusting! NEVER AGAIN (and honestly, I see in the reviews that I'm not the only customer they've treated this way). GENTLEMEN, BEFORE TRUSTING THIS "CLINIC", READ THE REVIEWS CAREFULLY (I can already imagine the excuses they'll give to clear their consciences in responding to this review; after all, that's what they've done with all the reviews, without ever making amends or apologizing).

My experience with the Polivet Clinic was unfortunately very negative, and I wouldn't recommend it today.

Giotto was 7 years old. I had already been there in 2020 and had a good experience, which is why on August 15th, when he began to feel very ill, I decided to take him back there with confidence.

On the 15th, severe kidney failure was diagnosed. During the night between the 15th and 16th, Giotto's condition worsened: he vomited and also showed melena. On the 16th, the possibility of poisoning was considered, despite my having explained that he lived mostly at home and that I considered it unlikely. Only on the 17th was he diagnosed as positive for leishmaniasis.

And here I am left with many questions: given such a serious situation, why wasn't this possibility explored earlier? And above all, why wasn't I already offered the option of transferring him to a better-equipped facility, including dialysis, on the 15th?

That day, Giotto was still alert, lively, responsive, and walking. Maybe he wouldn't have made it anyway, but I wanted to at least be able to try everything.

On the 17th, I asked for a transfer to another clinic to try dialysis. We also asked for a veterinary ambulance, but they explained that, since it was a holiday and staff were limited, it wasn't available. So, I started calling myself to find one.

The doctor, however, told me there was no need to wait for the ambulance, because Giotto had "gone out for a walk" and could be transported by car.

When I went down to take him, however, Giotto was barely walking. I transported him by car as instructed. Upon arrival at the new clinic, his temperature was around 40°C, and I was told he was suffering from hyperthermia/heat stroke.

During his hospital stay, I also found him completely soiled with his own feces several times, including his muzzle, face, and leash, and I cleaned and sanitized him myself.

I understand that a clinic has other animals to care for and that organizing on holidays can be more complex. But if I bring my dog ​​to a clinic, pay for hospitalization and even the holiday supplement, I expect him to be guaranteed dignity, hygiene, and care. If the facility, due to staffing shortages or other limitations, was unable to adequately care for such a serious case, I would have preferred to know immediately and be referred elsewhere.

And I want to make this clear: it's not about money. I would have paid any amount and gone anywhere to give Giotto every opportunity.

For me, Giotto wasn't "just a dog." He was family. And I believe that being a veterinarian means, first and foremost, wanting the best for the animal, even when that requires the humility to say: "We can do this here, but there are facilities better equipped than us. If you want to explore every possibility, take him there."

I would have preferred to hear that on the 15th, when Giotto was still alert and responsive, rather than arrive at the transfer when his condition had already deteriorated.

Giotto died on August 18th.

I can't know if an earlier transfer or a different treatment would have saved him. Perhaps the outcome would have been the same. But if there was even one more chance, I would have wanted to be able to give it to him.

We could have at least tried. And today I can't help but wonder if, had I given him that chance earlier, my love would still be here with me.

From the beginning we felt welcomed and the testing, the appointments, the prescriptions and the kindness were always quick and easy.
We thank you so much for your kindness and understanding to our particular situation.
We highly recommend this veterinary medical center to anyone looking for excellence in medical care.
Special thank you to Dr. Elisa Corsi and Dr. Valentini the oncologists in charge of our precious angel.  To the nurse staff and the administrative staff  as well.

From the receptionists, who are unique, professional, and special, even on a human level, to the nurses and doctors, Polivet is excellent! My Goliath had to undergo a devastating operation, and I was cared for by all the staff from the very first moment! Excellent is an understatement! Debora Alberici

My boots clinic... It's the only emergency room open 24/7. On August 15th, a cat was hit in front of me. Needless to say, I called the police, but they didn't give me a damn. So I called them, knowing they were the only ones who could help me. Instead of giving me the chance to take it to them (obviously not at my own expense, but more importantly, I couldn't have done much because I had to leave; I know they'd have bled me dry), they basically left me hanging, letting it die. I watched it fade away, breath after breath, effort after effort. That cat wanted to live, and they left it to its fate... Disgusting... but why are you even swearing? I cried the whole trip (I should point out that I had a car and would have rushed to take it to someone who could save it). Needless to say, I felt so bad afterwards. I watched it fade away in my hands...

We brought our hamster last night after it was bitten on the leg by our dog. We weren't familiar with the clinic, as it was in the province, but given the time, we went straight to take him there. We had a great experience; the doctor was both humane and professional; she took care of him, providing him with the necessary first aid and therapy! We don't know how it will go, but thank you so much for your help. We're confident our gypsy will be back doing parkour in his cage for a long time to come!

I highly recommend this clinic, which I wasn't familiar with. I had an emergency with my 4-year-old dog due to poisoning or something similar, and they amazed me with their expertise, professionalism, passion, and kindness. The facility is large, clean, and well-equipped. The atmosphere is very warm and professional. Congratulations to the entire team, especially the sonographer Valentina Scafetti. All the best to everyone!

Dear Madam,
We're sorry to see your negative review, especially considering that Molly was discharged after overcoming a very delicate medical situation and that we've already scheduled her follow-up appointment for next week.
We're happy that our team was able to help you and we sincerely hope that Molly continues to feel well. If there were any aspects of your experience that you weren't satisfied with, we'd be happy to listen and discuss them directly.

Thank you so much for your review from all the Polivet staff! 😊

Our bunny, Cookie, had a urinary incontinence problem in July, and Dr. Ranno immediately diagnosed the problem and prescribed follow-up tests that confirmed her diagnosis, then prescribed antibiotic therapy. Every time we've had a problem, she's always found the best solution. Truly unbeatable!

I come regularly for my two bunnies, Cookie and Supplì. The veterinary center is highly competent, always available for both checkups and emergencies. The receptionists are fantastic, especially Caterina, who always gives us a warm welcome. Dr. Ranno, who has just saved Cookie from a particularly complicated intestinal operation, and Dr. Gallucci, who took Cookie in when he was feeling ill, are second to none. She did her utmost to provide the most accurate diagnosis possible.
